text:
marta: Heads-up — a customer hit failures on embeddings after switching models a few hours ago. Getting 400s with 'dimension mismatch'. They report bulk uploads time out too. Can someone triage? :rotating_light:

samir: Can you paste the error blob and the exact request they sent (headers + body)? Also which model name did they use?

marta: Error payload from proxy: ```HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
{
  "error": "Embedding vector length 4096 does not match model dimension 1536"
}```
They say model param was `rwd-embed-1536` in their UI, but client code uses an internal model alias `open-emb-large`. They uploaded a precomputed vector set as a single JSON array per request. I suspect a client-side batch/format mixup.

diego: Quick questions:
- Are they sending `input` as array of strings, or array of vectors?
- Any X-Forwarded headers or proxy altering payloads?

marta: They claim `input` is array of precomputed vectors (float lists), not raw text. Example body they sent: ```{
  "model": "open-emb-large",
  "input": [[0.1,0.2,...,0.0],[...]]
}```
But server says expected 1536 and got 4096.

samir: Hypothesis: `open-emb-large` is actually mapped to new 4096-dim model in our catalog, while `rwd-embed-1536` is 1536. If client's UI showed `rwd-embed-1536` but backend alias resolved differently, that's an aliasing bug. Also possible they concatenated vectors (e.g., batching client appended vectors into one long vector).

ingest-bot: Ingest pipeline traces for recent failing requests (trace ids):
- trace=trc-abc123 (model=open-emb-large, content-type=application/json)
- trace=trc-abc124 (model=rwd-embed-1536)
(see https://console.redwood.ai/traces/trc-abc123)

marta: Customer provided curl repro (sanitized):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-embed-1536","input":[[0.1,0.2, ... ,0.0]]}'
```
They say it fails intermittently; sometimes it succeeds, sometimes dimension error.

samir: Intermittent suggests routing/caching mismatch. Possible scenarios:
- Upstream routing sometimes maps alias to the 4096 model (rollout gone wrong)
- Client library sometimes serializes as text (string) vs array, and our parser treats string length as tokenization? less likely.

ops: I pulled the route config — there was a canary rollout of `open-emb-large` on 2026-03-12 that maps alias `open-emb-large` -> model-v2 (4096). Canary weight 10% in region-us-west. If the customer's alias resolution uses the alias, that explains intermittent.

marta: Oh — customer UI showed the old name but their token resolves alias server-side. So when requests hit canary hosts they get 4096 model. That produces dim mismatch when client still sends 1536-vectors.

diego: For observability — how do we get per-request latency and span breakdown for embeddings route? Customer is also complaining of high p95 and batch timeouts.

samir: Use the trace link from ingest-bot. To capture detailed spans next time, ask customer to include header `X-RWD-Debug: 1` in their request (one-time) and give us the `trace_id` that comes back in `X-RWD-Trace` response header. That enables request-level breakdown: parse/tokenize/kv-cache/compute/postprocess. Example breakdown from a failing trace: ```parse: 8ms
tokenize: 35ms
kv_lookup: 10ms
compute: 310ms
quantize_post: 12ms
response_serialize: 5ms
TOTAL: 380ms```

marta: Customer also saw high latency when sending large batches (200 items). They use 512 batch_size in client library but server saw single huge payload. Any best-practice guidance?

samir: For embeddings, recommended client batching: send raw text inputs as arrays up to payload size ~1MB or 64 items depending on model. If sending precomputed vectors, the vectors must match model dim. Don't wrap multiple vectors into one top-level vector. Server expects `input` to be an array of elements where each element is either a string or a vector of correct length. If you need to send 200 items, split into multiple requests or use asynchronous ingestion route. Also check `Content-Encoding` — some clients gz compress incorrectly which can corrupt counts.

marta: Actionable triage checklist for support to collect from customer before escalation:
1) 3 raw failing request bodies (sanitized) + success sample if available
2) Response headers including `X-RWD-Trace` and full error body
3) Model name string they used in the client config and any alias mapping in their UI
4) Approx timestamps (UTC) for failures
5) If they used precomputed vectors, one example vector (comma-separated)

diego: I'll add a dashboard card for immediate visibility: `support/embeddings/dim-mismatch` showing counts by model alias, p50/p95 latency, and 400 error rate by error message.

deploy-bot: Canary config note — canary `open-emb-large` -> model-v2 (4096) currently at 10% in us-west. Manual rollback command: `rwdctl rollout rollback --alias open-emb-large --to stable`

samir: Next steps (owners):
- diego (Support): collect artifacts from customer and paste here.
- ops: temporarily set canary weight to 0 while we confirm and notify the customer.
- samir (Eng-ML): verify alias catalog mapping and add sanity-check on vector upload that includes header `X-Expected-Dim` validation to return early helpful error.

marta: Customer is onboarded to enterprise — they want SLA-level update. I'll mark as P1 and notify account team. Diego I'll DM you the customer logs.

diego: Got the logs, uploading now. For quicker debug, customer gave trace id `trc-abc123`. I looked up trace: it shows resolution path: alias->canary host->model-v2. I'll attach the raw trace export to the ticket.

samir: I pushed a tiny validation patch to reject precomputed vectors whose length doesn't match the model at the API gateway layer. It returns a clearer error now: `400 InvalidEmbeddingDimension: expected 1536 but got 4096. Check model alias and input vectors.` We'll roll to canary in staging.

ops: I set canary weight to 0 for open-emb-large in us-west and notified infra. Watch the metrics for error rate drop.

marta: Thanks all. Support to send customer ETA: we will pause canary and follow up in 1 hour with root cause and mitigation steps.

samir: Also note — for long-term observability, add a per-route trace sampling for embeddings=0.5 so we have more examples for these issues.

marta: Closing thread for now, will reopen if errors persist after canary rollback. Thanks :thumbsup:
